standards.title: Repository Naming
standards.summary: Patched-source repositories use a consistent `patch-<reponame>` name in the finos-osera GitHub organization.

requirements.text: Patched-source repositories must live in github.com/finos-osera unless the working group approves an exception.

checks.title: Repository is in the finos-osera organization

requirements.text: Patched-source repositories must use the prefix patch- followed by the upstream repository or artifact name.

checks.title: Repository name uses the patch prefix

standards.title: Patch Branches
standards.summary: Patch providers use `patch/<version>` source workflow branches for every supported major or minor line.

requirements.text: Patch providers must create version-scoped source workflow branches using patch/<version>.

checks.title: Supported line has a patch version branch

standards.title: Baseline Tags
standards.summary: Every patch line identifies its unpatched starting source SHA with a `v<VERSION>+patch.baseline` tag.

requirements.text: Patch providers must tag the unpatched baseline source commit using v<VERSION>+patch.baseline.

checks.title: Baseline tag exists and resolves to a commit

standards.title: Open Source Patch Publication
standards.summary: Patched-source repositories should be fully public, hosted in the appropriate official fork, and released under the same open-source license terms as the original code.

requirements.text: Patched-source repositories must be fully public and publicly fetchable without private credentials.

checks.title: Repository is publicly fetchable

requirements.text: Patched-source repositories must preserve applicable upstream open-source license files and notices and release patched source under the same applicable license terms as the original source line.

checks.title: Upstream license terms, files, and notices are preserved

requirements.text: Patched-source repositories must be hosted in the appropriate official OSERA fork for the upstream project or artifact line.

checks.title: Repository is the appropriate official OSERA fork

standards.title: Patch Basis Classification
standards.summary: Providers distinguish upstream backports from provider-developed fixes for each CVE or fix item carried by a patch release.

requirements.text: Patch providers should classify whether each CVE or fix item in a patch release is based on an upstream fix, an adapted upstream fix, or a provider-developed fix, using a vocabulary still to be defined by the working group.

checks.title: Patch basis classification is present

standards.title: Upstream Provenance Links
standards.summary: Backports link to the upstream commit or advisory that introduced the fix being carried back.

requirements.text: Backport evidence must link to the upstream commit, commit range, pull request, advisory, or release note defining the fix.

checks.title: Upstream provenance link is present

requirements.text: Backported commits carrying upstream-authored code should name the upstream commit and include a Co-authored-by trailer for the upstream author where applicable.

checks.title: Upstream authorship trailer is present where applicable

standards.title: License Headers for New Files
standards.summary: New source or test files match the prevailing license format of the surrounding project.

requirements.text: New source or test files added by a patch must follow the prevailing license-header convention of the surrounding project.

checks.title: New files use the local license-header convention

standards.title: Provider Test Provenance
standards.summary: Test execution methods are provider-dependent, but the provider publishes a unit-test report artifact for recipients to understand release validation.

requirements.text: Patch providers must publish test provenance for the patched artifact, including the tested commit, a test command or suite that runs at least the tests the fix's commits added or changed, runtime when relevant, test report, and passing test result.

checks.title: Test provenance is recorded

requirements.text: A release that changes no source in its repository, only the versions its build pins and the OSERA plumbing files, must record as its test provenance the release it pins that carried the fix, whose own test provenance passed.

checks.title: A release that changes no source names the tested release it carries

standards.title: Bytecode Compatibility
standards.summary: Patched artifacts preserve the bytecode level of the last released artifact unless an explicit exception is approved.

requirements.text: Patched Java artifacts must preserve the bytecode level of the last released artifact unless an exception is approved.

checks.title: Bytecode level matches the prior released artifact

standards.title: Patch Version Naming
standards.summary: Patched releases use package-ecosystem-appropriate version naming profiles that optimize recipient tooling outcomes before choosing a concrete syntax.

requirements.text: Official OSERA patched releases must use the applicable package-ecosystem patch version naming profile, or the default SemVer 2.0-compatible OSERA form where no concrete profile exists, so supported package resolver, dependency update, repository manager, SCA, feed, and policy tooling can identify the patched artifact as the latest applicable remediation on the same upstream version line.

checks.title: Applicable patch version naming profile is selected

requirements.text: Release tags, artifact versions, vulnerability feeds, and release evidence must carry the same patched-release identifier.

checks.title: Release identifier is consistent across source, artifact, and feeds

standards.title: Java Patch Version Naming
standards.summary: Java patched releases use a version naming profile that optimizes Maven, Gradle, repository-manager, dependency-update, SCA, feed, and policy-tool behavior for the affected upstream version line.

requirements.override-explanation: Specializes the generic applicable-profile rule with a Java-specific version convention. The CARE-style convention uses the OSERA identifier; the parent obligations to identify the latest applicable remediation on the same upstream line and preserve baseline and OSERA identity remain.
requirements.text: Official OSERA Java patched releases must use the ratified Java patch CARE-style version naming convention with the OSERA identifier, so supported Java resolver, dependency update, repository manager, SCA, feed, and policy tooling treats the patched artifact as the latest applicable remediation on the same upstream version line.

checks.override-explanation: Replaces generic profile-selection evidence with Java profile-decision, resolver, and dependency-update compatibility evidence. The parent consumer outcome remains the acceptance criterion; the naming convention is the CARE-style OSERA form described below.
checks.title: Java patch version pattern passes supported tooling compatibility tests

requirements.override-explanation: Specializes the parent identifier-consistency obligation for Java artifacts by explicitly including Maven package URLs. The same patched-release identity must still connect source tags, artifacts, feeds, and evidence.
requirements.text: Java release tags, artifact versions, Maven package URLs, vulnerability feeds, and release evidence must carry the same Java patch version identifier.

checks.override-explanation: Uses Maven package URL evidence for the parent consistency check while retaining release-tag, artifact-version, and feed identity matching.
checks.title: Java release identifier is consistent across source, artifact, and feeds

requirements.explanation: Specializes the generic applicable-profile rule with a Java-specific version convention. The CARE-style convention uses the OSERA identifier; the parent obligations to identify the latest applicable remediation on the same upstream line and preserve baseline and OSERA identity remain.

Specializes the parent identifier-consistency obligation for Java artifacts by explicitly including Maven package URLs. The same patched-release identity must still connect source tags, artifacts, feeds, and evidence.

checks.explanation: Replaces generic profile-selection evidence with Java profile-decision, resolver, and dependency-update compatibility evidence. The parent consumer outcome remains the acceptance criterion; the naming convention is the CARE-style OSERA form described below.
Uses Maven package URL evidence for the parent consistency check while retaining release-tag, artifact-version, and feed identity matching.

standards.title: Approved Producers
standards.summary: Official OSERA signed artifacts are produced only by producers approved for the targeted standards pack.

requirements.text: Official OSERA signed artifacts must identify a producer that appears in the approved-producer registry for the targeted standards pack. Each producer record must contain id, contact, github_users, staging_account, pgp_fingerprint and pgp_key_urls, with a unique id matching the producer identity in release evidence and fitness results.

checks.title: Producer is approved for the targeted standards pack

requirements.text: The producer identity used at publication time must be recorded in the fitness result and release evidence, as an exact-string match of the registry entry's id. The fitness result and the verdict must also record the registry entry's staging_account and github_users as copied from the registry, and separately the observed release-tag actor. The observed upload account may be null in the CI fitness result because the gate observes it at upload time; this null value does not fail the CI check. The gate must record the observed upload account in the verdict. In 0.1.0 a difference between the copied account metadata and the observed actors is recorded and does not block.

checks.title: Producer identity is recorded in release evidence

standards.title: Artifact Publication Hygiene
standards.summary: Published OSERA artifacts include consistent package metadata, checksums, and repository evidence required by the publication gate.

requirements.text: Official OSERA artifacts must publish expected package files and checksums for the ecosystem being released.

checks.title: Package files and checksums are present

requirements.text: Published package metadata must identify the patched version consistently with REL-003.

checks.title: Package metadata uses the approved patched version

standards.title: Patch Request Authorization
standards.summary: Patch releases should trace to an approved backlog item, request, sponsor record, or equivalent authorization record.

requirements.text: Patch releases should identify the backlog item, public request, sponsor record, or equivalent authorization record for the patched coordinate and line.

checks.title: Patch request authorization evidence is present

standards.title: Build Provenance and Signed Attestation
standards.summary: Producers should sign an attestation linking the published artifact digest to the source tag, build process, SBOM, VEX, test evidence, and license audit.

requirements.text: Producers should sign an attestation linking the artifact digest to the source tag and build provenance.

checks.title: Signed build provenance attestation is present

requirements.text: The attestation should reference SBOM, VEX, test evidence, and license audit material for the release.

checks.title: Attestation references release evidence bundle

standards.title: Build Security Scanning
standards.summary: Patch release builds should be checked for build-tool, dependency, and pipeline-injection risks before publication.

requirements.text: Patch providers should run build-security scanning appropriate to the package ecosystem before publishing an official patched artifact.

checks.title: Build-security scan evidence is present

requirements.text: Build-security evidence should identify unresolved high-risk findings or explain why the selected tooling is not applicable to the patched project.

checks.title: Build-security findings are dispositioned

standards.title: Coordinated Remediation Adoption
standards.summary: Providers publish versioned remediation sets and supported adoption procedures so consumers can resolve the intended patched dependencies without reconstructing transitive dependency overrides themselves.

requirements.text: Providers must declare the supported dependency scope, upstream baselines, applicable ecosystem profile, and consumer entry points and tooling configurations for adopting a remediation set.

checks.title: Supported scope and adoption entry points are declared

requirements.text: Providers must publish an immutable, versioned remediation set identifying exact artifact versions and associated remediation evidence, and disclose the dependency changes, validation performed, and known limitations for adoption.

checks.title: Versioned remediation set identifies exact artifacts and evidence
Dependency changes and validation scope are disclosed

requirements.text: Providers must publish a supported adoption procedure that avoids consumers having to author and maintain artifact-by-artifact transitive dependency overrides, verify that it resolves the intended remediations for the declared configurations, and report when those remediations cannot be resolved.

checks.title: Supported adoption procedure is published
Adoption resolves the intended remediations in supported configurations

standards.title: Java Line Release and BOM Propagation
standards.summary: A patched artifact releases with every artifact in its line, and every supported BOM that pins the line releases again pinning the new version, so a recipient takes the fix by advancing one BOM version.

requirements.override-explanation: Specializes the supported-scope declaration with Java lines, upstream baselines, member repositories, and pinning BOMs. The inherited adoption verification check records supported consumer entry points and tooling.
requirements.text: Patch providers must publish a line declaration in the line's repository naming the BOM or the artifact set that defines the line, its members, the patch repository each member is released from, its upstream baseline, and the supported lines whose BOMs pin it.

checks.override-explanation: Checks the generic scope declaration against Java upstream BOMs and artifact sets; supported consumer configurations are also recorded by inherited REL-009.CHECK-006.
checks.title: Line declaration is present and complete against the upstream baseline
Every member's repository is a patch fork of the upstream that ships it

requirements.override-explanation: Specializes publication of an immutable remediation set by releasing every Java line member at a coordinated version, with checksums and pedigree. The inherited change-disclosure check preserves the generic evidence obligation.
requirements.text: A patch must release every member of its line at the line's next patched version, whether or not each member changed, shipping unchanged members as the upstream bytes with rewritten metadata.

checks.override-explanation: Checks the generic versioned remediation set through coordinated Java artifact versions, checksums, and pedigree.
checks.title: Every line member is published at the release version, unchanged members byte for byte

requirements.override-explanation: Specializes the supported adoption procedure with bottom-up BOM propagation to every supported root. The inherited adoption verification check also verifies the resolved consumer result.
requirements.text: After a line releases, every supported line whose BOM pins it must release at its own next patched version, with the BOM pinning the new version and no other managed version changed, bottom-up until every supported root has released.

checks.override-explanation: Checks the Java BOM pin changes that implement the generic adoption procedure. Inherited REL-009.CHECK-006 verifies consumer resolution, while the added root check verifies propagation completeness.
checks.title: A BOM release pins the current release of every supported line it manages and changes nothing else
The fix has reached every supported root

standards.title: OpenVEX and CycloneDX Feeds
standards.summary: OSERA-compatible providers contribute patch data to both OpenVEX and CycloneDX feed formats.

requirements.text: OSERA-compatible releases must be represented in OpenVEX and CycloneDX feed data.

checks.title: OpenVEX and CycloneDX entries exist for the release

requirements.text: Feed entries must preserve the exact patched package URL, including encoded release metadata.

checks.title: Feed purls match the published patched artifact identifier

standards.title: Change and Test Surface Guidance
standards.summary: Providers publish concise recipient guidance describing what changed and what surface area should be tested.

requirements.text: Patch providers should publish versioned recipient guidance describing what changed and what surface area should be tested.

checks.title: Recipient guidance uses the current guidance schema

standards.title: Estate-Wide Patch Application
standards.summary: Patch feeds should support automated discovery and application across dependency estates.

requirements.text: Patch feeds and metadata should support estate-wide discovery and application across dependency estates.

checks.title: Estate-wide discovery metadata is present

standards.title: Standards-as-Code Source Metadata
standards.summary: OSERA standards use human-authored Markdown with structured YAML front matter as the machine-readable source of truth.

requirements.text: Standard pages must include schema-versioned YAML front matter containing identifiers, lifecycle status, requirements, checks, evidence expectations, and pack references.

checks.title: Standard front matter validates against the active OSERA schema

requirements.text: The standards repository must publish normalized catalog artifacts generated from the Markdown front matter.

checks.title: Generated catalog artifacts are current
